subject: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)
thread_body:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

Hey Nikhil —

We’re ready for Hosted API product review on the template adoption telemetry plan before we lock it in for internal beta and then public launch.

Goal
- Tag template-generated traffic so we can build a clean activation funnel + retention metric set (time-to-first-success, ongoing usage, support deflection).
- Keep it privacy-safe and low-cardinality.

Proposed approach (v1)
1) Client-side opt-in tag on requests (templates only):
   - Header: X-Redwood-Template: rag-agent
   - Header: X-Redwood-Template-Version: 0.1.0
   - Optional: X-Redwood-Template-Run-Id: <uuid> (for correlating initial setup flows)

2) Server-side: gateway whitelists the above headers (strip anything else), normalizes values (known template names only), and emits analytics event(s).

3) Events (high level)
- template_request (counts requests, latency distributions, model, response status)
- template_first_success (first 200 from template within 30 minutes of init)
- template_error_category (mapped from template error taxonomy, e.g. auth/quota/network/tool/retrieval)

Privacy & safety guardrails (draft)
- No user identifiers in headers.
- No prompt, tool args, or retrieved content in any telemetry. (Existing request logging policies still apply; templates also add redaction in logs by default.)
- Template Run ID is random UUID; not tied to account/user.
- Values are validated to avoid accidental high-cardinality.

Questions for Hosted API sign-off
1) Are you OK with the header names? Any conflicts with current gateway behavior?
2) Are you OK with Template Run ID in v1, or should we defer?
3) Any constraints from proxies/corp environments re: unknown headers?

Attachments:
- template-telemetry-tagging-plan-v1.pdf
- quickstart-templates-launch-metrics-v0.3.xlsx

Thanks —
Monica
DevEx Engineering Lead


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 10:01 AM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

Thanks Monica.

Generally in favor, but I want to be careful here given we’re going to document this publicly and it’ll get copy/pasted into real apps.

Concerns / asks:
1) “Opt-in” needs to be unambiguous. If templates default to sending these headers, it’s effectively opt-out. I’m OK with “default on in the template”, but we should:
   - document clearly how to turn it off
   - ensure “off” is truly off (no hidden fallback tags)

2) Corporate proxies: I’ve seen issues where non-standard headers get blocked. If this causes 4xx or “mysterious network errors,” it’ll backfire.
   - Do we have a plan if headers get stripped/blocked? (E.g., do we degrade gracefully?)

3) X-Redwood-Template-Run-Id: I’m not convinced we need this in v1. It’s easy to say “random UUID,” but in practice it becomes a correlation handle. I’d prefer to ship without it unless there’s a strong reason.

4) Header values: We should constrain aggressively (enum list) and ensure they can’t be used to smuggle data.

If you can update the proposal with the above + a recommended default posture for public launch, I’ll sign off.

Nikhil
PM, Hosted API


---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 11:18 AM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

All makes sense.

On your points:

1) Opt-in vs default-on
- Our current plan: default ON in templates for internal beta only.
- For public launch: we can flip default to OFF (config/env), or keep default ON but make the disable path prominent.

My preference: default ON for public launch, BUT only when the user sets REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1 during setup (so it’s explicit).

2) Corporate proxies
- Good call. We’ll add try/catch around request creation + a “header strip retry” path (if request fails at gateway/proxy with header-related 4xx, retry once without telemetry headers).
- We’ll also document a “if behind a corporate proxy, disable telemetry headers” troubleshooting entry.

3) Run ID
- We can drop Run ID from v1. We still get adoption metrics from template name + version + standard account/workspace IDs on our side.

4) Value validation
- We’ll only allow a fixed set of template names (rag-agent, rag-api, etc.) and semantic versions.
- The gateway will reject/ignore unexpected values and won’t forward arbitrary headers.

I’ll send an updated PDF today and update the metrics sheet accordingly.

Monica

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 12:07 PM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

Jumping in from docs side — if we go with “explicit enable” (REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1), we can make it very clear in:
- README “Telemetry (optional)” section
- Docs page: “How we measure template success” + privacy note
- Troubleshooting: “Corporate proxy blocks custom headers”

Also suggest a short callout: “Do not put user IDs/emails in any template tags; Redwood ignores unknown values.”

Elliot
Docs Lead


---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 4:46 PM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

Updated proposal (summary; I’ll swap the attachment in the thread tomorrow after I regenerate it):

Decision changes based on your feedback:
- Remove X-Redwood-Template-Run-Id entirely from v1.
- Telemetry tagging becomes explicit enable:
  - Env: REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1 (default 0)
  - When disabled: templates do not send any telemetry headers.
- Add resilience:
  - If request fails with a header-related error (proxy/gateway), templates will retry once with telemetry headers stripped.
  - Add a clear log line: “Template telemetry disabled due to header rejection; set REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=0 to silence.”

Headers (v1)
- X-Redwood-Template: rag-agent
- X-Redwood-Template-Version: 0.1.0

Gateway expectations (per Brian’s earlier note in standup)
- Explicit whitelist; unknown headers dropped.
- Values normalized to enum list; unknown values ignored and do not get indexed.

Privacy note
- No prompt/tool args/retrieved docs included in telemetry.
- We’ll add README warning: don’t repurpose these headers for app-level identifiers.

If you’re OK with this, we’ll proceed and wire to the Console filter work.

Monica


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 26, 2025 at 9:23 AM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

This is much better.

Conditions for Hosted API sign-off:
1) Explicit enable only (REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1). Default must be disabled.
2) No Run ID in v1.
3) Gateway must whitelist + validate values (enum); anything else is dropped.
4) Retry-without-headers behavior should be bounded (1 retry) and not create loops.
5) Docs must include:
   - what’s collected (and what is NOT)
   - how to disable
   - corporate proxy troubleshooting

If those are met, you have my sign-off.

Nikhil

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 26, 2025 at 5:38 PM
Subject: Re: Template adoption telemetry + privacy review (Quickstart Templates v1)

Confirmed on all 5 conditions.

Action items we’re taking this week:
- Update template code paths to require explicit enable + implement single bounded retry without headers.
- Update README + docs pages (Elliot/Wei pairing) with the collection/disclosure section and proxy troubleshooting.
- Coordinate with gateway work to enforce whitelist + enum validation.

I’ll reply here once the updated doc is uploaded and linked in PM-912.

Monica
